answer: Before any fault, each key signs with its own quill a fixed-form independence claim, a sonnet whose locked stanzas name its operator root, committed on-ledger at submit height. When keys sharing one root fail together in an epoch, settlement reads those committed claims and burns every co-signer's bond. A hollow claim sworn by shells under one hand both adds a bond and raises the odds some shell faults and drags the rest down, so expected loss climbs faster than clone count. Honest keys fault idiosyncratically and keep their stake, and the burn stays non-poolable across cooperating operators.
